resources.string: PatchManul finds ESP32-S3 pedal controllers on your Wi-Fi network and opens their web interface, so you do not have to remember IP addresses. It shows what is there — it does not control the devices.\n\nThe firmware on those devices is Builty\'s Controller, an open-source project of its own. This app is a separate companion to it: it is neither part of that project nor endorsed by it.

This app is open source. The source code and ready-made releases are available here:

This app collects no data about you and sends nothing to third parties.

• Only the favourites you create yourself are stored, with name, IP address and — where known — the name from DNS. They stay on the device: the app is excluded from the system backup, so its data does not end up in a cloud backup either. The price is that favourites have to be created again after changing devices.
• Network requests go to addresses on the local network only, in order to find devices and check whether they are reachable.
• To obtain device names, queries are sent to the DNS server configured on the Wi-Fi network — as a rule the router itself.
• There is no usage analysis, no advertising is embedded, and no crash reports are transmitted.
• A device's web interface is shown in a WebView. What happens there is up to the device, not to this app; in doing so, the WebView may store data from the page shown on the device.

The app requests three permissions, all for the same purpose — reaching the devices on your own Wi-Fi network:

• Network access, to query the devices and show their web interface.
• Access to the network state, to read the device's own address and the netmask. Only from these does it follow which range of addresses has to be searched.
• Access to the local network. From Android 17 on this is a separate permission the system asks about explicitly; without it the devices stay out of reach.

No location permission is required.
